subject: Post-call: runbook sprint, HW compatibility & procurement path for private (air-gapped) deployment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novabio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: runbook sprint, HW compatibility & procurement path for private (air-gapped) deployment

Claire, thanks for the time today — great convo. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) High-level outcome: Novabio is leaning toward a Private (air-gapped) deployment to satisfy regulatory controls and data residency. Key constraints you flagged: intermittent on-site maintenance windows, strict change approval for firmware, and an HSM requirement for key storage.

2) Action items we agreed on: 
- Redwood to share an appliance spec sheet + recommended BOM for a single-site starter (attached: appliance_spec_sheet.pdf).
- Novabio to run internal procurement check and confirm whether you want Redwood-managed hardware procurement vs. a customer-procured model. I included a short doc with procurement paths (attached).
- Schedule a 2-hour "runbook sprint" with your Ops + Security to map maintenance cadence, patch approval process, and emergency rollback playbook. Proposed times below.

3) Questions we still need answered to finalize scoping: 
- Expected offline patch cadence (monthly/quarterly/other?) and who signs off on security patches.
- Physical access policy for on-prem engineers and whether sealed transports are required for devices.
- Any pre-approved vendors for rack/server hardware if you prefer customer procurement.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
A) Site-survey template (I attached a lightweight spreadsheet) — please fill environmental details (rack space, power PDU per rack, network isolation, NTP access, physical courier restrictions) and return by EOD Thurs.
B) Runbook sprint: Wed 07/26 or Thu 07/27, 10:00-12:00 PT. Confirm a slot and attendee list.

I'll hold a short internal sync with Marissa and Priyom tomorrow to align the technical checklist before the sprint.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: appliance_spec_sheet.pdf (PDF), redwood-procurement-path.md (MD), novabio-site-survey-template.xlsx (XLSX))

From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novabio.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@novabio.com>, Novabio IT <it@novabio.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook sprint, HW compatibility & procurement path for private (air-gapped) deployment

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Patch cadence: Security will want quarterly windows for non-critical patches; emergency security patches may be applied outside of windows but require a 24-hour notification and SOC approval.
- HSM: We have an internal HSM vendor (SafeKey) and would prefer integration with a customer-managed HSM, but we'd like Redwood to confirm compatibility and outline the integration checklist.
- Physical access: Our sites require escorted access and signed NDAs for any Redwood field engineer visits.

We've started filling the site-survey template — attached a partially completed version with rack/power info. We can complete the rest after confirming the expected network egress points (if any).

Runbook sprint: Thu 07/27 10:00-12:00 PT works for our Ops and Sec team. Attendees: Claire Zhou (SRE lead), Tom Ellis (Infrastructure), Priya Kapoor (Security — will forward official invite).

I'll also loop in procurement once we've reviewed the procurement-path doc. Thanks for attaching the BOM; one quick ask — can you flag which line items are optional vs. mandatory for 24/7 inference SLA?

Best,
Claire
Infrastructure Lead
Novabio
(Attachment: novabio-site-survey-template-complete-partial.xlsx (XLSX))

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novabio.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook sprint, HW compatibility & procurement path for private (air-gapped) deployment

Looping in a few technical clarifications ahead of the sprint — I attached a short MOP checklist and preliminary BOM review notes. Highlights: 

- HSM integration: Redwood supports PKCS#11-compatible HSMs and can run in a customer-managed HSM model. We'll need endpoint connectivity for the HSM admin interface during initial onboarding (can be routed via a temporary jump-host per your security rules).
- Firmware/patch process: For air-gapped installs we provide an offline patch bundle and instructions. Typical cadence we support: quarterly regular bundles + urgent patches. We can include a cryptographic signed manifest for all patch artifacts to satisfy your audit requirement.
- Optional redundancy: We recommend an N+1 appliance if you require 99.9% availability during maintenance windows. Minimum starter configuration is single-appliance for evaluation (lower cost) with planned upgrade path to N+1.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-mop-checklist.pdf (PDF), benchtop-bom-notes.md (MD). I'll call out optional vs mandatory items in the BOM: core inference appliance, redundant power supplies, and an HSM line are mandatory for your compliance ask; GPU count and burst cache storage are size-dependent and optional for starter config.

See you on Thu for the sprint — I'll have a one-page rollback playbook ready to review.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-onprem-mop-checklist.pdf, benchtop-bom-notes.md)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novabio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@novabio.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: runbook sprint, HW compatibility & procurement path for private (air-gapped) deployment

Thanks everyone — confirmed for Thu 07/27 10:00-12:00 PT. Final prep checklist for Novabio to get the most out of the sprint: 

1) Complete site-survey (even partial values are useful) and return by Tue 07/25 EOD.
2) Confirm whether procurement will be Redwood-driven or customer-driven so we can finalize pricing and lead times.
3) If you want Redwood to validate HSM compatibility ahead of the sprint, please share vendor model & admin contact (we'll treat it as sensitive).

I'll send the calendar invite and include a short agenda: kickoff + scope, maintenance/patch policy alignment, HSM integration requirements, procurement and logistical constraints, and an action log with owners.

Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachments referenced above)"
